what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat two conditions: (1) Dupuytren's contracture, which is a condition where the tissue under the skin of your palm thickens and tightens, causing one or more fingers to bend toward your palm and making it hard to straighten them; and (2) Peyronie's disease, which is a condition in men where scar tissue forms inside the penis, causing it to curve and making erections painful.
how_to_take: This medicine is NOT something you take by mouth or give yourself at home. It is an injection (a shot) that must be given by a specially trained doctor in a medical office or clinic. For Dupuytren's contracture, the shot is given directly into the thickened cord in your palm or finger. For Peyronie's disease, the shot is given directly into the scar tissue (plaque) in your penis. Your doctor will tell you exactly what to expect during each visit and what to do afterward, including any finger exercises or penile modeling procedures.
dosing: For Dupuytren's contracture: You will receive one injection of 0.58 mg into the affected cord. About 1 to 3 days later, you will return to the doctor's office for a finger extension procedure to help straighten the finger. This counts as one treatment cycle. You may need up to 3 treatment cycles per cord, with each cycle spaced about 4 weeks apart. For Peyronie's disease: You will receive 2 injections per treatment cycle, given 1 to 3 days apart, directly into the penile plaque. Each treatment cycle is separated by about 6 weeks. You may have up to 4 treatment cycles. Your doctor or their staff will also show you how to do penile modeling (gentle straightening exercises) at home after each cycle.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by your doctor in a clinic, it is important to keep all of your scheduled appointments. If you need to cancel or miss an appointment, call your doctor's office as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to make up for a missed injection on your own.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. Your doctor's office handles all storage. The medicine must be kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) and must not be frozen. It should be used within a certain time after it is prepared, so your healthcare team will manage this carefully.
what_to_avoid: Do not try to forcefully straighten your finger or bend your penis on your own right after the injection without your doctor's guidance, as this could cause injury. Avoid strenuous activities with the treated hand for at least 4 weeks after each treatment cycle for Dupuytren's. For Peyronie's disease, avoid sexual activity for at least 2 weeks after each pair of injections. Do not take blood-thinning medicines (like warfarin, aspirin, or ibuprofen) without talking to your doctor first, as they can increase your risk of bruising and bleeding at the injection site. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: sudden severe pain in the treated area; a popping or snapping feeling in your finger or hand after the injection; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness, or rapid heartbeat; numbness, tingling, or loss of feeling in your finger; broken skin, blisters, or open sores at the injection site; signs of infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, or pus; or, for Peyronie's disease, difficulty urinating, severe bruising, or a painful erection that will not go away.
when_it_works: Results vary from person to person. For Dupuytren's contracture, many patients begin to see improvement in finger straightening within a few days to weeks after each treatment cycle, following the finger extension procedure. For Peyronie's disease, improvement in penile curvature may be seen after completing several treatment cycles, which can take a few months. Be patient and continue all follow-up visits. Your doctor will monitor your progress throughout your treatment.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: This medicine is not approved for use in people under 18 years of age. Older adults: No special dose changes are needed based on age alone, but your doctor will monitor you carefully. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not intended for use in women. However, women of childbearing age who may be exposed should tell their doctor immediately. Kidney or liver problems: No specific dose adjustment is required, but always inform your doctor of any health conditions you have.
